title: Per-model composite SLI matrix and error-budget orchestration policy
creator: Asha Patel
description: Define a standardized, per-model SLI matrix (latency, availability, and quality) and a graduated error-budget response choreography that ties SLI breaches to concrete automated and manual mitigations (circuit breakers, regional failover, load-shedding, and rollbacks). Deliverables: SLI definitions and computation queries, dashboards, alert thresholds, playbook for automated actions, and implementation tickets for telemetry and control-plane hooks.
acceptance_criteria: SLI spec doc published with prometheus/exemplar queries for latency (p50/p95/p99), availability (success rate by status code), and quality (model-specific hallucination/accuracy metric)
Error-budget policy table mapping % burn rate to actions (alerts, throttles, circuit-breaker trips, failover thresholds, canary rollbacks)
Console dashboard prototype showing per-model composite SLO, current burn rate, and projected time-to-breach
Automated circuit-breaker prototype that can: 1) detect sustained p95 latency > threshold for 3m; 2) trip and divert a configurable % of traffic to fallback variant; 3) emit structured audit events
tasks: Draft SLI taxonomy for all model families (seq-to-seq, decoder-only, embeddings)
Instrument quality SLIs: integrate eval hooks and offline prompt-sets to compute continuous quality score
Create Prometheus/metrics queries and exemplars for each SLI
Build console widget for composite SLO and burn-rate timeline
Implement control-plane webhook for policy-driven traffic diversion and circuit-breaker state changes
End-to-end test: simulate regional outage and validate failover choreography and observability
decisions: Use composite SLO that weights latency, availability, and quality per-customer-importance instead of single-metric targets
Quality SLI will be model-class specific; for generative models we will use hallucination-rate + top-1 semantic-similarity for labeled prompt sets
Error-budget windows: rolling 30-day window for long-lived services and 1-hour for immediate incident detection (short-term burn)
risks: Quality SLI can be noisy for new models — risk of frequent false positives; mitigations: require 3x sample confirmations and combine with human review before irreversible actions
Automatic failover may increase egress cost in multi-region scenarios; require budget guardrails in Dedicated/Private customers
Circuit-breaker false trips could reduce availability unnecessarily; adopt graded throttles and traffic mirroring for validation before diversion
